newsitem.title: IRAQ: Russia wants more from Iraq's oil deal with U.N..
newsitem.headline: Russia wants more from Iraq's oil deal with U.N..

text.p: A visiting Russian minister complained on Tuesday that Russian companies had failed to get enough sales under Iraq's oil-for-food formula with the United Nations.
Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said his visit was to help Russian firms boost exports to Iraq of humanitarian supplies parallel to the increased amounts of Iraqi crude Russia was buying.

"Russian companies have undertaken an active role in buying Iraqi oil...but there is something strange in the way coordination and cooperation is being carried out in the supply of humanitarian goods to Iraq by these companies.
"Here we register that Russian firms have not achieved good success so far," Rodionov told an Iraqi-Russian joint committee in Baghdad.

Under the U.N. agreement worth $2 billion each six months, Russian firms have contracted to buy 26.2 millon barrels of oil in the six months from December 1996 when Iraq's oil started flowing to international markets for the first time in six years.

Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Mohammed Rasheed said President Saddam Hussein had ordered Iraqi ministries "to give absolute priority to friends, in the forefront of them Russia, in the selling of Iraqi crude or buying of humanitarian goods."

Rodionov said Russian leaders appreciated Saddam's "decisive political decision". He hoped current talks would enable the two sides to "lay down necessary measures to increase the role of Russian companies in supplying Iraq with humanitarian goods."
Rodionov said Russia was interested in selling spare parts for power stations, silos and oil installations. Iraq has earmarked more than $100 million of oil money for electricity and oil repairs.

Of $2 billion from oil sales over six months, Iraq will have an estimated $1.3 billion after funneling 30 per cent to a fund for Gulf War reparations and meeting other U.N. costs. More than $800 million has been earmarked for food.
The Russian Foreign Trade Ministry said on Thursday its organisations were interested in selling Iraq 100,000 tonnes of wheat, 50,000 tonnes of sugar and other foodstuffs.
In 1995 the two countries signed an agreement under which Iraq pledged to give Russian firms a major share in developing its oil industry and oilfeilds.
Russia supports lifting all curbs on Iraqi oil exports and hopes Iraq would be able to repay debts worth billions of dollars.
